name: KAISER
description: Kaiser is a beloved Canadian trick-taking game, historically popular in Saskatchewan and the Prairie provinces. Played by four players in partnerships, it uses a unique 32-card deck featuring two highly consequential cards: the 'Kaiser' (3 of Spades, worth -3 points) and the 'Bonus card' (5 of Hearts, worth +5 points). It is a game of high variance and strategic 'dumping' of negative points.

content.text: Kaiser is a beloved Canadian trick-taking game, historically popular in Saskatchewan and the Prairie provinces. Played by four players in partnerships, it uses a unique 32-card deck featuring two highly consequential cards: the 'Kaiser' (3 of Spades, worth -3 points) and the 'Bonus card' (5 of Hearts, worth +5 points). It is a game of high variance and strategic 'dumping' of negative points.

Originating in the Ukrainian-Canadian communities of Saskatchewan in the early 20th century. Its name and mechanics are likely related to European games like 'Skat' or 'Euchre' brought by Central European immigrants.
32 cards: 7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A in all suits, BUT the 7 of Hearts is replaced by the 5 of Hearts (+5), and the 7 of Spades is replaced by the 3 of Spades (-3).
